title: Fix integer overflow on hostile H.264/HEVC parameter sets
author: Pedroj-64
body:
## What and why

`BitReader::read_ue()` can return up to `u32::MAX`, so `read_ue()? + N`, `log2_min + read_ue()?` and the crop / conformance-window arithmetic in the H.264 and HEVC parsers overflowed. That is a panic in debug builds and a silent wrap in release: e.g. `pic_width_in_mbs_minus1 = u32::MAX` wrapped to a width of 0, which passed the `<= 1024` check.

- `bitstream`: add `BitReader::read_ue_plus(n)`, an overflow-checked `ue(v) + n` returning `InvalidExpGolomb`.
- `h264` / `hevc`: use it for every `read_ue()? + N`; saturate the `log2_*` size sums (the existing range checks then reject them); validate the H.264 crop in `u64`; make HEVC `crop_rect` saturating; validate the HEVC RPS delta range before casting to `i32`.

Found by mutation-fuzzing the decoders with synthetic SPS / slice data.

## How it was tested

- 4 regression tests (`read_ue_plus_rejects_overflow`, two `hostile_sps_values_are_errors_not_overflows`, `hostile_st_rps_deltas_are_errors_not_overflows`); I checked they fail on the previous code and pass now.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test, assets, layers pass. `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes for the touched crates.

title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger (only the web build does, via `WebLogger`), so every `log::warn!` / `log::error!` is discarded, including the crash guard's panic report in `crates/engine/src/guard.rs`. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue, and `RUST_LOG` can't help them.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere.

## What

`apps/deckcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (just `log`):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `logs/deckcraft.log` next to `ui.json` and `prefs.json` (Linux `~/.config/deckcraft/logs/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/DeckCraft/logs/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\DeckCraft\logs\`). `prefs_path` is split into `config_dir()` + `prefs_path()`.
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `deckcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512); without a usable directory the buffer is released.
- **Levels:** `info` for `deckcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable directory or a failed write keeps standard error only; lock poisoning is handled.

`main.rs`: the logger is installed first; the file is attached after argument parsing so `--version` creates nothing. The `eprintln!`s for `--sample` and files that fail to open go through `log::error!`; `control_server.rs` logs its bind/listen messages.

title: macOS DMG: branded window background and icon layout
author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![DeckCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/deckcraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the DeckCraft colour field, DeckCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small DeckCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

## How

Same approach as PhotoCraft's and VectorCraft's, which have landed (storytold/photocraft#1201, storytold/vectorcraft#493):

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg`: the source. Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.
- `background.tiff`: 1x 660×400 + 2x 1320×800 in one HiDPI TIFF (16-colour palette, Deflate, sRGB; 18 KB). No paper grain: noise doesn't compress, and this keeps the binary small.
- `dmg-layout.DS_Store`: Finder's view settings (window 660×400 content, icon size 128, DeckCraft.app at (326, 205), Applications at (574, 205), the background). It's named so it isn't mistaken for, or ignored like, a Finder-generated `.DS_Store`.
- `generate.py`: writes both from the SVG on any OS (`pip install 'pillow>=12' ds_store==1.3.3 mac_alias==2.2.3`, resvg on PATH). The output is byte-for-byte reproducible and carries nothing from the machine that ran it: no paths, users, disk names or volume UUIDs.

title: Slide show: a click after a long pause plays its step instead of skipping it
author: alexanderalber
body:
## Bug

In the slide show, clicking to play an animation step after waiting on the slide longer than that step's duration made the step finish immediately: everything appeared at once, without animation. Clicking quickly worked, which made it look tied to the transition into the slide (it is not: it reproduces with Fade and when starting the show on the slide itself).

Repro with the sample deck: start the show on slide 4 ("From the Sun to your sky"), wait ~4 s, click. Expected: the boxes zoom in one after another. Actual: all appear at once.

## Cause

In `show.rs` the step clock ran before the frame's input actions were applied. A click produced `PlayStep`, `ShowState` was already `playing`, but `step_start` was still the time the slide was entered, because `apply` sets it afterwards. So `t_step >= step_duration` and the clock pushed `step_done` in the same frame.

## Fix

Apply the input actions before reading the step clock (7 lines). Actions the clock itself produces are applied afterwards, as before.

## Checks

- `cargo xtask ci` green.
- Drove the running app over the control channel (`show.start`, `ui.key`, `ui.inspect`), polling the show state every 250 ms after the click: before the fix the step jumped to its end within 250 ms after a 3–4 s pause; after it the step takes its ~1 s, both when entering via a transition and when starting on the slide. Checked a mid-step screenshot.
- No automated test: the logic lives in the egui `ui` function; a test would need a UI harness. Happy to add one if you have a preferred way.

title: Tables: rows grow to fit their text, cell text in the PDF text layer (#13)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #13.

What happened: some tables store row heights of 0 (`<a:tr h="0">`). pandoc and python-pptx write them like this. DeckCraft drew all the rows of such a table on top of each other. `deckcraft-cli convert` also left the table text out of the PDF text layer.

What changed:

- Drawing, double-click to edit a cell, and the cell outline while editing all use these heights.
- `place_slide` now lays out table cell text, so table text is in the PDF text layer.

Tests:
- `render::tests::table_rows_of_zero_height_grow_to_fit_text`: a pandoc-style table with `h="0"` rows. Each row gets a height, the rows stack one below the other, a taller stored height is kept, and the placed text of each cell is in the right row.

title: Default Windows startup to DirectX 12
author: DWAA1660
body:
No DeckCraft issue reports this yet. This is a preventive fix for the same Windows startup crash.

Same fix as storytold/designcraft#168, applied to DeckCraft. FilmCraft has the same change for storytold/filmcraft#179.

## Problem

DeckCraft's desktop app uses eframe's default wgpu instance, which enables `PRIMARY | GL` on Windows. Creating the OpenGL backend can crash inside AMD's OpenGL driver (`atio6axx.dll`) before adapter selection or any Rust error handling runs. The app then flashes in Task Manager and exits with no window and no error (storytold/designcraft#167, storytold/filmcraft#179, storytold/filmcraft#268). `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` was the verified workaround.

## Change

- New `apps/deckcraft/src/graphics.rs`: when no `WGPU_BACKEND` is set, the Windows wgpu instance enables only DirectX 12 before it is created, so OpenGL is never initialized as a fallback. Picking an adapter afterwards would be too late.
- `main.rs` applies it on Windows only. An explicit `WGPU_BACKEND` is still honoured, and the process environment is not changed.
- macOS, Linux and the web build are unchanged.
- README: a short Windows troubleshooting note on the default and the `WGPU_BACKEND` override.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p deckcraft graphics`: 2 passed. `windows_default_initializes_only_dx12` asserts that eframe's default includes GL and that the configured instance is DX12 only. `explicit_backend_override_is_preserved` covers overrides.
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` (Linux): clean. `rustfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- `cargo check -p deckcraft --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`: clean, so the Windows-only call site compiles.
- Limitation: no Windows/AMD hardware here, so the driver crash itself was not reproduced. The DX12 workaround comes from the designcraft report.

title: PPTX: recognise packages whose [Content_Types].xml is not in the first 4 KB
author: wurstbrotdlx
body:
## Problem

`deckcraft_pptx::sniff` searched only the leading 4096 bytes for `[Content_Types].xml`. OOXML writers may place that part anywhere in the archive, and recent PowerPoint builds (16.x) store it as the **last** zip entry, megabytes into the file. Every such deck was rejected with "not a presentation DeckCraft can read" even though `import` handles it fine.

Measured on a real folder of 300 `.pptx` files: 169 (56 %) had the part beyond the 4 KB window and failed to open. Re-packing one of them with the part moved to the front made it load; moving it back past 4 KB made it fail again, so the sniff window is the only cause.

## Fix

Look the part up in the zip's central directory instead of scanning the prefix (one `ZipArchive::new` + `index_for_name`, no decompression).

## Test

`crates/pptx/tests/sniff.rs` re-packs the sample deck with `[Content_Types].xml` last, behind 64 KB of padding, and asserts that it is recognised and imports; a second test keeps the negative cases (empty, `PK` only, PDF, plain zip). The positive test fails on `main` and passes with this change.

`cargo test -p deckcraft-pptx`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-pptx --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean locally.

title: Start screen: theme tiles that wrap to a new row keep the left inset (#17)

title: Morph: a changed geometry morphs its outline (a circle turns into a star)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Follow-up to #5. Paired Morph shapes that differ only in geometry (another preset, other adjust values, a custom path) and possibly fill colour no longer cross-fade: one shape moves and its outline turns from the old geometry into the new one.

## How

- **`geom::morph`** (new) aligns two outlines the way manim does: the same number of contours, the same number of cubic curves per contour pair, then every control point moves in a straight line. On top of that:
  - closed contours are turned and reversed so the points travel least (a triangle does not twist on its way into a circle);
  - extra points go to the longest curves;
  - a sub-path without partner grows out of (or shrinks into) a point, so a cube's faces appear and a donut's hole closes;
  - when a pair differs in fill mode, outline or fill rule, the looks cross-fade: a fill only one side has fades out or in (a filled shape turning into a line), and when both fill, the even-odd side lies underneath and the other fades over it (the donut's hole fills smoothly).
  - The start-point search is capped, so very long custom paths stay cheap per frame.
- **`anim::morph_frame`** lists such shapes in `MorphFrame::paths`.
- **`render`**: `PathMorph`, a new `render_blend` argument next to `TextMorph`; `geometry_shape` draws those shapes with the morphed geometry. Both outlines are built at their own sizes, so the alignment does not change while the box grows. `stroke` takes an alpha for the fades.
- **`show.rs`** maps the frame's paths, as it does for texts.

The path morph is ported from my own presentation framework alexplain (MIT).

## Tested

- `cargo xtask ci` green (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).
- New tests: path alignment, refinement, no twisting, unpaired sub-paths, scaling into the current box, fades, hostile input (empty, NaN, zero-size) in `geom`; pairing rules in `anim`; in `render`, the first and last frame match the old and new slide, and a fill only one side has is half there halfway.

title: Issue #61: Shapes: flipped shapes keep their text readable
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #61.

Flips mirror a shape's geometry, never its text. Labels on flipped shapes were drawn mirrored (flipH) or mirrored upside down (flipV), e.g. "Next" on a left arrow made by flipping a right arrow.

As in PowerPoint, flipH text now stays upright, and flipV (or both flips) turns it 180°. Rotation and flipped groups are handled the same way.

- New `render::text_transform(m, tr, rotation)`: when the overall transform is a reflection (the shape's own flip or a group's), it mirrors the text back about the text rect's centre, then applies vertical-text rotation. The text rect keeps its flipped place.

title: Links: Insert Hyperlink with a bare caret inserts the address; the show follows links (#31)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Closes #31.

"Saving does nothing and they don't function" had three separate causes. Saving the file was not one of them: links round-trip through `.deckcraft` and `.pptx` (checked).

### 1. Insert Hyperlink with a bare caret changed nothing
With the caret at a word boundary (end of the text, after a space, empty paragraph), `insert.hyperlink` called `format_run` on an empty range: the dialog closed and nothing happened. Now, as in PowerPoint, the address is inserted at the caret as linked text in the surrounding formatting (email links without `mailto:`, slide links show the slide's title; a new optional `text` param overrides). A selection or a caret inside a word links that text as before.

Typing right after a link no longer extends it (`unlinked_at_link_end`), otherwise "insert the address, keep typing" would link the rest of the sentence.

### 2. The slide show ignored links
Nothing in the show read `Hyperlink` actions; only the PDF export did. A click on a link now follows it through `ShowState::follow` (`deckcraft-anim`): slide, next/previous/first/last, Last Slide Viewed, End Show, URLs. The click areas come from `deckcraft_render::place_slide(..).links`, the same ones the PDF export uses; a text link wins over its shape's action. The pointer turns into a hand over a link. Custom show, program and media actions aren't followed yet.

### 3. URLs never opened on desktop
The app's eframe was built without the `links` feature, so `ctx.open_url` was a no-op natively (this also affected the ribbon's app page link). Enabled as in DesignCraft, EffectCraft and PrintCraft. This adds `webbrowser` and `url` to `Cargo.lock`.

title: Slide show: transitions show the old slide instead of the new one twice (#33)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Closes #33.

**Cause:** in `Show::apply` (`crates/ui-egui/src/show.rs`), a slide change stored `self.tex.as_ref().map(|(_, t)| t.clone())` as the transition's old picture. That clones the *handle*; the next frame renders the new slide with `h.set(..)` into the very same texture. Old and new were then the same image, so every transition blended the new slide with itself and looked like an instant change. Morph was not affected, it renders into its own texture.

**Fix:** take the old texture out of `show.tex` (`self.tex.take()`), so the new slide is loaded into a texture of its own while the transition still holds the old one. One line plus a comment.

**Test:** `show::tests::a_transition_keeps_the_old_slide_in_its_own_texture` applies a slide change with a fade and checks the transition keeps the old texture and `show.tex` no longer points at it. Fails on `main`.

**Verified on Windows 11:**
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).
- In the app via the control channel, red slide → blue slide with a 6 s fade, screenshot 2 s in: `main` shows pure blue `(0, 0, 255)`; with the fix `(163, 0, 92)`, a real cross-fade. A 6 s Push shows the blue slide pushing in from below over the red one.

Note: this touches the same lines in `show.rs` as #45 (links in the show); whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase, which I'll do.

author: shuff57
body:
## Visual equation editor

Insert → Equation used to be a one-line text field that swapped a few tokens for Unicode and inserted an italic text box. This replaces it with a real equation object and an editor where you type into the formatted math (`x`, `^`, `2` shows a raised exponent immediately).

### What it adds
- **`deckcraft-math`** (new layer-1 crate): math tree, OMML reader/writer (unknown elements preserved as raw XML, bounded against hostile input), linear-text parser/exporter, template catalogue, and a caret/selection editing model.
- **Commands:** `insert.equation`, `equation.update`, `equation.get`, `equation.templates`, `equation.fromLinear`, `equation.type`. Equations are stored as `RunKind::Math` OMML and round-trip through PPTX. The importer now sets run text via `to_linear(from_omml)` and keeps run properties.
- **Layout:** TeX-style 2-D layout in `deckcraft-text` (fractions, roots, scripts, big operators with limits, delimiters, matrices); Math runs are inline atoms that keep character/caret counts.
- **Editor dialog:** template palette, live preview, in-place typing with caret and selection (`^ _ /`, `sqrt`, Greek names, symbol shortcuts, auto-paired brackets), undo/redo, copy/cut, Tab between places. Double-click on an equation reopens it. The linear text field remains as a secondary path.

### Known limitations
- Radical and bracket fit is rougher than KaTeX; the real fix is a math-capable OFL font (STIX Two / Latin Modern Math) via craft-fonts. Noted in ROADMAP.md.

This adds a print path that goes straight to the browser's native print dialog instead of forcing a download first:

- `Services::print`, a web-only hook (PDF bytes in, system print dialog out), alongside the existing `download` hook
- `SlideApp::print_now()`, which builds the PDF via the engine's `cmd::file::pdf_bytes` (the same lowest-level function `file.export` already uses under the hood) and hands the bytes to the hook
- `Ctrl`/`Cmd+P` wired up in `ui_shortcut` — doesn't collide with the existing `Ctrl+Shift+P` command palette shortcut
- a "Print…" entry in the File menu, right after "Export…"
- the web runner's `print` service implementation: PDF bytes → `Blob` → object URL → hidden `<iframe>` → `iframe.contentWindow().print()` once the iframe has finished loading

## Why

Export-only means every print is a round trip through the OS's file picker and PDF viewer just to get to a print dialog. This skips straight to it, the same way Word/Excel/PowerPoint's own Ctrl+P does.

Mirrors the same feature already added to WordCraft (storytold/wordcraft#209) and GridCraft (storytold/gridcraft#143).

## Testing

Built with `trunk build --release`, deployed, and smoke-tested in Firefox: Ctrl+P and File → Print… both open the system print dialog on the current presentation's PDF.

title: Morph: align an outline morph once per transition, not every frame
author: alexanderalber
body:
Follow-up to #27, as suggested when it landed.

`render_blend` built a `GeometryMorph` (contours plus alignment) for every morphing shape on every frame, although only `t` and the current box change while a transition plays. The `Renderer` now keeps the aligned morphs in a `morph_path::Cache`, keyed by both geometries and their own sizes. At the end of each `blend` it drops the ones that frame did not use, so the cache empties when the transition ends.

- render: `morph_path::Cache` replaces `morph_path::geometry`; `blend` sweeps it after the frame.
- test: `morph_path_aligns_once_per_transition` (one alignment across frames, same geometry as a fresh one, emptied after a frame without morphs).

## How much it saves

Small. Measured with a throwaway test (release build, one morphing shape, 960x540 at scale 1, single run each, not committed):

| Morph | rebuild per frame (before) | cached | whole frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| ellipse -> star5 | 11.0 µs | 0.8 µs | 765 µs |
| rect -> star32 | 40.6 µs | 1.7 µs | 794 µs |
| heart -> cloud | 9.6 µs | 0.7 µs | 731 µs |

So the alignment step gets about 14 to 24 times cheaper, which is roughly 1 to 5 % of a frame; rasterising dominates. It matters more with many morphing shapes at once. Two different transitions rendered alternately on the same thread rebuild each time, which is no worse than before.

`cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: macOS: open presentations from Finder, the Dock and `open -a`
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## Problem
- **Finder never offers DeckCraft.** DeckCraft declares its file types but no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, so Finder doesn't offer it for a `.deckcraft` or `.pptx`, in Open With or on double-click.
- **`open -a` doesn't open anything.** `open -a DeckCraft deck.pptx` starts the app without opening the presentation. LaunchServices sends the path as a `kAEOpenDocuments` Apple event, which winit 0.30 doesn't handle.

## Fix
- **`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`:** DeckCraft owns `.deckcraft`. It's offered at Alternate rank for `.pptx`, `.potx` and `.ppsx`, the PowerPoint formats File > Open reads, so it doesn't take over the user's default app for them.
- **`apps/deckcraft/src/apple_events.rs`:** registers the handler with the audited [`fmv-macos-events`](https://crates.io/crates/fmv-macos-events) crate (pinned `=0.1.0`), which PdfCraft and PhotoCraft already use. The Objective-C interop stays inside that crate (the workspace forbids `unsafe`), and winit's delegate is left alone.
  - Each frame drains the queue. Paths go through `SlideApp::open_path`, the same as the command line, and an error shows in the status bar.
  - A quit event closes the window.
  - The registration lives in `main()` until the event loop returns, so the event that launched the app is caught too.

## Testing
Tested on macOS (Apple silicon) with a full `packaging/macos/package.sh` build installed in /Applications:
- [x] `open -a DeckCraft deck.pptx` with the app not running: the presentation opens.
- [x] `open -a DeckCraft other.deckcraft` while it's running: it opens as a second document.
- [x] An Apple-event quit closes the app.
- [x] LaunchServices lists DeckCraft for `.pptx`; the existing default (Keynote) stays the default. DeckCraft is the default for `.deckcraft`.
- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: File: Close asks before discarding unsaved changes (#60)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #60.

## Problem
#344 (File tab) added `app.closePresentation`, which asks before closing a presentation with unsaved edits. File › Close in the File view and ⌘W now run it. The command palette still lists the engine's `file.close` as well, so it shows **Close** twice. If you pick the engine's `file.close` entry, an edited presentation is closed without a prompt.

## Fix
- **The palette leaves out `file.close`** (`menus::palette`). Its one **Close** is now `app.closePresentation`, which asks Save / Don't Save / Cancel when there are unsaved changes.
- **`file.close` itself is unchanged.** It still never opens a dialog, so scripts, the control channel's `engine.execute` and MCP close without asking, per AGENTS.md ("programmatic calls never open dialogs").

This PR first added its own `app.close` command, close dialog and ⌘W/File-menu routing. #344 shipped the same behaviour, so those parts were dropped when merging `main`, leaving just the palette fix and its test.

## Testing
- [x] Regression test `close_asks_before_discarding_unsaved_changes` (kittest), covering:
  - the palette lists Close once, and with unsaved edits it opens the close dialog instead of closing;
  - Cancel keeps the presentation and its changes;
  - a clean presentation closes at once;
  - `file.close` never shows a dialog.

  With the palette filter removed, the test fails (`the palette lists Close once`: 2 vs 1).
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- [x] `cargo test --workspace`: 775 passed, 3 failed. The same 3 fail on `main` in the same environment; they depend on installed fonts (`symbol_font_characters_draw_in_the_sym_font`, `ime_tests::korean_composes_in_the_notes_pane`, `ime_tests::cjk_text_in_the_interface_is_drawn_with_real_glyphs`).

title: Fonts: a lookup finds an installed family whichever thread loads it first
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes the flaky engine test `tests::clicks_in_flipped_shapes_hit_the_text_where_it_is_drawn`. On `main` (d556ff9), `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --release` failed it in about 1 run in 3, always with `left: [(0, 1), …]` vs `right: [(0, 2), …]`. Run alone, it always passed.

**Cause.** The test's text asks for Inter. When Inter isn't bundled (a craft-fonts checkout without `fonts/latin-manifest.txt`), `FontDb::face` falls back to installed fonts: Helvetica Neue, then Arial, each loaded the first time it's needed. Other tests load the same families at the same time through `system_fallback`, and two races in `FontDb` made the result depend on timing:

1. `try_family` only looked again when its own `load_cataloged` added faces. If another thread had added them first, it fell back to the next family.
2. A family's files were added one at a time, so a lookup could see part of a family. Arial's "Arial Bold Italic.ttf" sorts first, so "Regular" came back bold italic.

Logging a failing run showed it: the first click was laid out in Arial Bold Italic and the later ones in Helvetica Neue Regular. The different advances moved x=240 from character 2 to character 1.

**Change** (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`):
- Installed fonts load under one `loading` lock. A thread that waited checks whether the family is now loaded before reading any files. `load_cataloged` now returns whether the family is loaded, not whether this call added it.
- `add_fonts` adds all of a load's faces in one write, rechecking for duplicates under the lock. `add_font` calls it.
- `system_fallback` takes the same lock. If faces were added while it waited, it looks again, and it rechecks known misses. When only one thread is loading, it behaves as before.

### Tests (fails on `main`)
- fonts `concurrent_lookups_all_find_an_installed_family`: 8 threads resolve a family from a temporary font folder (Hack Regular, from `epaint_default_fonts`, already in `ATTRIBUTION.md`) at the same moment, on 20 fresh databases…

title: Command palette: one Export… entry that opens the dialog, no path-only duplicate (#79)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #79.

The command palette lists the engine commands and then the UI commands (`UI_COMMANDS`). Some labels exist in both lists. For "Export…", the engine `file.export` comes first and is selected by default. It needs a `path`, which the palette can't give, so Enter fails with ``invalid parameters for `file.export`: missing `path` ``. The second entry, `app.exportDialog`, opens the Export dialog.

The palette now hides an engine command when a UI command has the same label. Only the dialog entry is left. The same duplicates existed for:

- **Open…** (`file.open`) and **Save As…** (`file.saveAs`): they need a `path` too. The File menu and Cmd+O / Cmd+Shift+S already use the dialog commands.
- **Audio from File…** / **Video from File…** (`insert.audio` / `insert.video`): with no `path` or `data` they fail the same way.
- **Notes** (`slide.notes`): run from the palette with no `text`, it cleared the current slide's notes. The remaining entry is the Notes pane toggle (`view.notes`).

The engine commands are not changed. They still work through the control API and scripts. Only the palette list changes.

The list is built in a new `palette_items` function so a test can check it. The test checks that "exp" and "export" give one "Export…" entry, and that it is `app.exportDialog`. It also checks that each UI command is the only palette entry with its label. Both checks fail without the fix.

title: PPTX: animation rewind survives save and reopen (#77)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #77.

The PPTX writer (`effect_par` in `crates/pptx/src/write/timing.rs`) always wrote `fill="hold"` on the effect `p:cTn`, and the reader (`animations` in `crates/pptx/src/read/timing.rs`) never set `Animation::rewind`. So "Rewind when done playing" was lost on every PPTX save and reopen, for any effect.

PowerPoint stores that option as `fill="remove"` on the effect's `p:cTn`, so the fix uses PowerPoint's own representation instead of reporting the setting as unsupported:
- export writes `fill="remove"` when `rewind` is on, and `fill="hold"` (as before) when it is off;
- import sets `rewind` when the effect node has `fill="remove"`, next to where it already reads `autoRev`, `accel` and `decel` from the same node.

Nothing else in the timing tree changes. The inner behaviour nodes keep `fill="hold"`.

Test: `animation_rewind_survives` in `crates/pptx/tests/roundtrip.rs` round-trips a Fade with rewind on and a Fly (with previous) with rewind off, then checks that rewind is still on for the first one and off for the second. Without the fix, the first one comes back with `rewind: false`.

title: PPTX: audio and video playback options survive a save and reopen (#74)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #74.

**Cause.** The PPTX writer (`media()` in `crates/pptx/src/write/shapes.rs`) wrote trim, fade and bookmarks into the `p14:media` extension, but no playback options. The reader (`pic()` in `crates/pptx/src/read/shapes.rs`) always set volume to 1.0 and left autoplay, loop and rewind false. After a PPTX round trip, `autoplay`, `loopPlay` and `rewind` came back false and volume came back as 1.0. Trim and fade survived, as the issue says.

**Fix.**
- Export writes the clip's playback options (volume, autoplay, loop, rewind, play across slides, hide while not playing, full screen) to one more `p:ext` in the picture's `p:nvPr/p:extLst`. The element is `mediaOptions` in a private namespace, `urn:deckcraft:media`. It sits next to the existing `p14:media` extension. PowerPoint skips `p:ext` entries it does not know, so the file still opens there.
- Import reads that element back. Files without it keep today's defaults (volume 1.0, all flags off).
- Linked (non-embedded) media lost these options in the same way, so the extension is now written for linked clips as well as embedded ones.

**What this does not do.** PowerPoint stores these options in the slide timing tree (`p:video`/`p:audio` with `p:cMediaNode`). DeckCraft does not write or read media timing nodes at the moment. So this change keeps the options across a DeckCraft round trip, but PowerPoint does not use them. Writing native timing nodes would be a much larger change, so I left it out of this PR.

**Tests** (`crates/pptx/tests/roundtrip.rs`)
- `pictures_media_and_ink_round_trip`: the embedded video in `rich_deck` now has autoplay, loop, rewind and volume 0.25 set, and the test checks they come back. Without the fix it fails (volume returns as 1.0, flags as false).
- `linked_media_keeps_playback_options` (new): a linked audio clip with autoplay, rewind and volume 0.5 keeps those values after the round trip.

title: Comments: browser-created comments and replies get a creation timestamp (#72)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #72.

`now()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs`, which dates both `comment.add` and `comment.reply`, returned an empty string on wasm because there is no `std::time::SystemTime` in the browser. So every comment and reply made in the browser build was saved with `date: ""`.

On wasm the seconds now come from the browser clock, `js_sys::Date::now()`. This is how `now_ms` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` already gets the time on wasm. The native path is unchanged. Both paths share the same `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` formatting, which now sits in a small `iso_utc` helper.

`js-sys` is added to the engine as a wasm-only dependency, the same way `ui-egui` declares it (`js-sys = "0.3"` under `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`). It is already in the lockfile, so nothing new is downloaded.

Tests (in `review.rs`):
- `timestamps_are_iso_utc` checks the formatting at the epoch and at the timestamp from the issue (`2026-10-10T13:10:35Z`).
- `the_clock_is_not_empty` checks that `now()` returns a dated string.

The unit tests run natively, so they cannot run the wasm branch itself. That branch is a single `js_sys::Date::now()` call that feeds the same tested formatter.

title: PPTX export keeps comment replies and resolved threads (#70)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #70.

The PPTX writer (`comments_xml` in `crates/pptx/src/write/mod.rs`) flattened every reply into a top-level `p:cm` and never wrote a status, so a PPTX roundtrip turned replies into separate comments and reopened resolved threads.

The writer now emits what the PPTX reader (`read_comments` → `one`) already parses:
- replies nest in a `p:replyLst` of `p:reply` elements under their parent, with the same depth limit (4) and per-list cap (1000) the reader uses;
- a resolved comment gets `status="resolved"`.

Author ids, `idx` numbering, dates and positions are written exactly as before; only the nesting and the status attribute are new.

Test: `comment_replies_and_resolved_state_round_trip` in `crates/pptx/tests/roundtrip.rs` round-trips a resolved thread with one reply plus an open thread. It checks two top-level comments, the reply under its parent, and both resolved states. Without the fix it gets three top-level comments, no replies and `resolved: false`.

title: Export: PNG images (all slides) in the browser downloads every slide (#64)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #64.

**Cause.** In the Export dialog, the native path passes `all` to `file.export`, but the browser path (no save picker, `services.download`) ignored it and always rendered `s.selection.slide`. So "PNG images (all slides)" downloaded the same single PNG as "PNG images (current slide)".

**Fix.** The browser image branch now goes through a small helper, `web_image_files`, that renders every slide when `all` is set and names the files `<name>1.png`, `<name>2.png`, ... It uses the same slide list, scale (2.0), encoders and file naming as the native `file.export` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`). Each file is handed to the existing download callback. The current-slide PNG, JPEG, PDF, PPTX and outline exports behave as before. The native desktop path is unchanged because it already handled `all`.

**Test.** `web_export_all_slides_gives_one_file_per_slide` builds a three-slide deck with slide 2 selected. It checks that the all-slides export gives `Deck1.png`, `Deck2.png` and `Deck3.png`, and that the current-slide export still gives a single `Deck.png`.

title: Paste: Ctrl+V pastes an image-only clipboard as a picture (#53)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #53.

**Cause.** `keyboard()` already turns an image on the clipboard into a picture, but only inside the `Event::Paste` arm, and that arm never runs for an image-only clipboard. In egui-winit 0.36 (`on_keyboard_input`), Ctrl/Cmd+V reads the clipboard as text. When there is no text it pushes no `Paste` event, and it `return`s before pushing the `Key` press event. So a screenshot or a picture copied from a browser or an image viewer reaches the app as nothing at all. Only the key **release** gets through, because egui-winit only swallows the press.

**Fix.** `keyboard()` keeps one flag (`v_seen`). A `Paste` event or a V key press sets it, and a V release clears it. If V is released and neither arrived since the last release, the press was a swallowed paste command, so the app reads `services.clipboard_image` and runs `insert.picture`, the same way the existing `Paste` arm does. The flag is updated before the "a text field has focus" early return, so a V typed into a text field is not later taken for a paste. Text paste is unchanged: its `Paste` event sets the flag, so its release does nothing. Modifiers are not checked on the release because users often let go of Ctrl before V.

This is only in the egui front end. The engine's `insert.picture` and the clipboard reader in `apps/deckcraft` are unchanged.

**Test.** `ctrl_v_pastes_an_image_when_no_paste_event_arrives` (kittest) sends the events egui-winit sends:
- a text `Paste` followed by the V release inserts no picture;
- a V release with no press or `Paste` before it (the image-only case) inserts one picture.

The second assertion fails on `main`.

title: Progress docs: re-measure against PowerPoint 16.113 (craftrules standard)
author: echelon
body:
Restructures DeckCraft's progress docs to craftrules `standards/progress-docs.md` and re-measures parity against **PowerPoint for Mac 16.113.4**. - Full parity: ~365–650 h. The earlier estimate was ~190 h; it left out localization, hardware, legacy formats, AI and the depth bugs users have since reported. The reconciliation is in `docs/target-app-parity.md`.

title: Linux: the title bar carries the window controls, as in PowerPoint
author: gyurix
body:
## What

On X11 the window manager draws its own title bar above the one the app already
has, so every window has two bars. Only the outer one carries minimize,
maximize and close, and it does not match the app it belongs to.

This turns the system frame off on Linux and FreeBSD and draws the controls in
the app's own title bar, which is where Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Acrobat put
them. The window still resizes, moves, maximizes and closes exactly as before.

## Why not leave the window manager's frame in place

It is not a matter of taste, in two places:

- **DeckCraft** draws the presentation full screen, and **PdfCraft** has a
  full-screen page view; in both, a system title bar would sit over the content.
- With client-side decorations the controls follow the app's own theme, so they
  stay legible in the dark theme instead of being a light bar on a dark window.

## How it was checked

Each app was built from this branch, installed as a `.deb` and driven with
`xdotool` on XFCE/xfwm4, 1920x1080:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| maximize / restore buttons | `_NET_WM_STATE` gains and loses `MAXIMIZED_HORZ`/`MAXIMIZED_VERT` |
| double-click on the title bar | same, in both directions |
| move by dragging the title bar | window moves |
| resize from all four edges | window resizes |
| resize from all four corners | window resizes diagonally |
| minimize, then reactivate | `_NET_WM_STATE_HIDDEN` set, then cleared |
| close | window closes, through the same unsaved-changes check |
| slideshow / full screen (DeckCraft, PdfCraft) | no controls drawn over the content |
| overlay screens (Backstage, palette) | controls stay reachable, drawn last |

## Compatibility

- macOS and Windows are untouched; both keep the system frame.
- `<APP>_SYSTEM_TITLEBAR=1` keeps the window manager's title bar, for anyone who
  prefers it or whose window manager needs a frame to place the window.
- The three new tooltip strings (`Minimize`, `Maximize`, `Restore Down`) are
  added to every f…

title: Linux: the display theme follows the desktop
author: gyurix
body:
## What

DeckCraft has no way to follow the desktop's light/dark setting: the interface
has a single on/off brightness, so it either matches the system by luck or never
does.

**Preferences… › Display theme** now offers *Use system setting*, *Light* and
*Dark*, with *Use system setting* the default.

## Why the second part is the important one

Adding a "follow the system" option is not enough on Linux. winit reports no
system theme there — `ActiveEventLoop::system_theme()` is `None` on every Linux
desktop — so the new option would have been a promise with nothing behind it,
exactly as it was in WordCraft and GridCraft.

So `desktop_theme` asks the XDG Desktop Portal's `Settings` interface for
`org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`, on a thread of its own so no D-Bus
call is ever made from the frame loop. That schema name is asked first because
GNOME's portal and XFCE's both answer it; the older
`org.freedesktop.interface.color-scheme` is asked second, which is the one KDE's
portal answers. The first answer is delivered straight away and the frame loop
drains it each frame, so switching the desktop theme while DeckCraft is running
is picked up within a few seconds. A desktop that answers neither leaves the
user's own choice standing.

macOS and Windows are untouched: winit answers there.

## No migration

The saved key keeps its name and its old meaning: a `ui.json` with
`brightness: "dark"` still reads as an explicit dark, and one with no
`brightness` key at all now means *follow the system*. `Dark Mode` on the View
tab keeps toggling between light and dark; the new setting is in Preferences.

`view.theme` is added alongside `view.dark` so an agent can set the preference;
an unknown value is refused rather than silently ignored.

## How it was checked

Built from this branch and run on XFCE with
`gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`:

| step | saved preference | drawn |
|---|---|---|
| fresh start, desktop dark | no `brightness` key | **dark*…

title: Linux: match the desktop scale instead of the panel's DPI
author: gyurix
body:
XRandR reports the panel's physical DPI while the desktop renders at 96, so winit scales every window up and the app looks zoomed for no reason. Pin WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR to 1 in the desktop launcher so menu and panel launches match the desktop.

Same fix as the local WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR=1 default; baked into the shipped launcher so installs work without system patches. Terminal launches can still export their own value.

title: Export: an unknown format is an error instead of a deckcraft file
author: mikl0s
body:
`file.export` with an explicit `format` outside the supported list (png, jpeg, jpg, pdf, pptx, potx, ppsx, deckcraft, outline, txt) fell through to the native deckcraft zip. A request for "docx" reported success and wrote a deckcraft archive under the requested name.

Before: `file.export {"format":"docx","path":"out.docx"}` over MCP returns `isError: false` with a byte count, and the file is a deckcraft archive, not a Word document.

Fix: an explicit unsupported format now returns an error naming the format and writes nothing. A format inferred from the file extension behaves as before.

Tests: new MCP test `export_rejects_unknown_format`.
- Without the fix: `cargo test -p deckcraft-mcp --lib` runs 5 tests, 4 pass and 1 fails (`isError` is false for "docx").
- With the fix: 5 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on the patched tree.

Made with Opus 5.5 high.

title: Slides: going to a slide that does not exist is an error
author: mikl0s
body:
`slide.go` clamped an out-of-range slide index to the last slide and reported success. A slide `id` that does not fit in u32 was also read as id 0 instead of being reported as an unknown slide.

Before: going to slide 99 of a two-slide deck lands on the last slide and returns success, so the caller cannot tell the move failed.

Fix: an index past the last slide is an error and the current slide stays where it is. A slide id beyond u32 reports "no such slide". Valid indexes, including the first and the last slide, work as before.

Tests: new MCP test `go_to_slide_out_of_range_is_error` (checks the first and last slide still work, that 2 and 99 are errors, and that a failed call does not move).
- Without the fix: `cargo test -p deckcraft-mcp --lib` runs 5 tests, 4 pass and 1 fails.
- With the fix: 5 passed, 0 failed; `deckcraft-engine` 42 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on the patched tree.

Made with Opus 5.5 high.

title: Commands: an invalid shape id is an error instead of the selection
author: mikl0s
body:
A shape `id` that was present but not a valid id (negative, not an integer, larger than u32) was treated as absent. Commands that fall back to the selection when `id` is missing, such as `text.set` and `text.edit`, then silently edited the selected shape instead.

Before: `text.set {"id": -1, "text": "x"}` returns success and rewrites whichever shape is selected.

title: Morph: a picture cropped differently on the next slide morphs its crop (#118)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Fixes #118.

Two paired pictures that differed only in their crop counted as changed content. The new picture therefore faded in over the old one on the moving box. Now they stay one picture whose crop morphs, which also covers a crop that changes together with the box.

How the crop is interpolated (`morph_crop`): on each slide, box + crop determine where the *whole* image lies. That image rectangle moves and scales linearly between the two slides, and each frame's crop is the part of it the interpolated box shows. Interpolating the crop fractions directly would make the image wobble whenever the box also changes. If one side's crop leaves nothing visible, the crop fractions are blended instead.

- `docs/animation-parity.md`: Morph row and revision history

Not covered: a picture whose crop **and** another property (adjustments, transparency) change still cross-fades as before.

author: alexanderalber
body:
Fixes #116.

**Cause:** the PPTX reader already turns PowerPoint's media effects (`presetClass="mediacall"`, `p:cmd playFrom/togglePause/stop`) into `AnimClass::Media` animations. I checked this with a synthetic PowerPoint-shaped timing tree: it gives `Media / play / OnClick` and `AfterPrevious`. The slide show never carried them out, though. Media started only through `autoplay` on entering a slide, or through a click on the media itself.

**Fix:**
- `Timeline::media_cues(step, from, to)`: the main-sequence media effects of a step that start within `(from, to]`.
- `Show` keeps a small media clock for the playing step. Each frame it queues the effects the step has reached, and `run_media_cues` carries them out: Play starts from the beginning unless the clip is already playing, Pause toggles, Stop stops. A step cut short by a click (`FinishStep`) still sets off its remaining effects. Going back sets off nothing.
- **Step length:** the play command's duration is the media's length (5 s video → 5 s step). Without a change, the next click during the video would only "finish" an invisible step, and you would need a second click to go on. Media effects now count with their start, not their end, toward the step's duration. `max_end` is unchanged, so an *After Previous* effect behind the video still waits for it, as in PowerPoint.

**Tests:**

title: PPTX import: a transition without spd is 0.5 s, not the effect's default (#117)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Fixes #117.

**Cause:** PowerPoint 2021 and 2024 write a 0.5 s transition with neither `spd` nor `p14:dur`. Both files attached to the issue have exactly this:

```xml
<mc:Choice Requires="p159"><p:transition><p159:morph option="byObject"/></p:transition></mc:Choice>
<mc:Fallback><p:transition><p:fade/></p:transition></mc:Fallback>
```

`"fast"` is the schema default of `spd`, so PowerPoint has nothing to write. The reader (`crates/pptx/src/read/timing.rs`) instead fell back to the effect's own default when `spd` was missing: Morph 2 s, Fade 0.7 s, most other effects 1 s.

**Fix:** a missing `spd` now reads as `fast`, 500 ms. `p14:dur`, `spd="med"` and `spd="slow"` behave as before. The writer is unchanged; it always writes `spd` and `p14:dur`.

**Tests:** `crates/pptx/tests/transition_xml.rs` exports a deck, splices transition XML into `slide1.xml` and reads it back:
- `powerpoint_half_second_morph_without_spd`: the XML from the issue's files gives Morph, 500 ms (2000 ms before the fix).
- `missing_spd_is_fast_for_a_plain_transition`: `<p:transition><p:fade/>` gives 500 ms (700 ms before).
- `spd_and_dur_still_apply`: `spd="med"` gives 750 ms, `p14:dur="1250"` wins over `spd="slow"`.

Both attached files also import with 500 ms on both slides through `deckcraft-cli convert`.

**Verification:** `cargo xtask ci` passes `fmt` and `clippy`. The `test` step couldn't finish locally because the machine ran out of commit memory while linking the workspace (os error 1455, unrelated processes). `cargo test -p deckcraft-pptx` and `-p deckcraft-engine`, the only crate that calls the importer, pass.

title: Charts: a single-series chart without an explicit title shows the series name as its automatic title (#142)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #142.

**Cause:** the chart reader (`crates/pptx/src/read/chart.rs`, `chart_from`) set `Chart.title` only from an explicit `<c:title>`. A chart with `<c:autoTitleDeleted val="0"/>`, no `<c:title>` and one series (the default python-pptx output in the issue) therefore had no title, while PowerPoint and LibreOffice draw the series name (`Sales`) above the plot.

**Fix:** after the series are read, if the chart has no `<c:title>`, `autoTitleDeleted` is explicitly `0`/`false`, and there is exactly one series with a non-empty name, the title is that series name. The renderer already draws `Chart.title`, so `render` (and the editor) now show it.

Kept narrow on purpose:
- An absent `autoTitleDeleted`, or one without `val` (schema default `true`), still gives no title. LibreOffice also treats a missing element as "deleted" for current Office files.
- Charts with more than one series keep no automatic title, as in PowerPoint.
- An explicit `<c:title>` and `autoTitleDeleted val="1"` work as before.

Saving is not affected for an unchanged chart. The writer compares a re-read of the kept XML with the model, and both go through the same `chart_from`, so the original part is still written back as it was.

Not changed: the issue says the reference title is bold. Explicit chart titles are not drawn bold either, so that is a separate rendering change.

**Tests:** three unit tests in `read/chart.rs`. `autoTitleDeleted=0` with one series gives the series name; `=1`, a missing element and two series give no title; an explicit title takes priority. The first test fails without the fix.

title: Charts: a missing varyColors varies single-series bar colours by point (#143)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #143.

A single-series column chart with no `<c:varyColors>` element (python-pptx writes it this way) rendered every column in accent 1. PowerPoint treats the missing element as "vary colours by point" and draws the columns in accent 1, 2, 3...

Two places were at fault:

- **Reader** (`crates/pptx/src/read/chart.rs`): a missing `<c:varyColors>` kept the model default `false`. It is now read as `true`, the schema default. An explicit `val="0"` still gives one colour.
- **Bar renderer** (`crates/render/src/chart.rs`): bars never looked at `vary_colors`. The new `bar_fill` gives each bar of a single-series chart with `vary_colors` and no series fill its own accent, using the same `series_color` as pie slices. It also uses a `<c:dPt>` solid fill for the point when one is set, the same way the pie renderer already does. Waterfalls are left as they were: the reader never produces them from a `<c:barChart>`, and their colours are not per point.

Charts with more than one series, or with an explicit series fill, look the same as before unless they have `<c:dPt>` point fills.

Tests:
- `read::chart::tests::missing_vary_colors_means_vary_by_point`: fails without the reader change.
- `read::chart::tests::explicit_vary_colors_is_respected`: `val="0"` and `val="1"` are still read as before.
- `tests::single_series_column_chart_varies_colours_by_point`: a single-series column chart draws differently with `vary_colors` on and off. Fails without the renderer change.

title: Charts: value axes start above zero when the values sit high, as in Office
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Related to #144.

## Context
This PR first fixed #144: the issue's data (42.1, 18.7, 6.3) drew 0–50 in steps of 10, where PowerPoint and LibreOffice draw 0–45 in steps of 5. Upstream ce1c7b7 ("Charts: axis number formats, automatic major unit, hidden axes") has since rewritten the value-axis scaling, and `main` now draws the issue's chart as 0–45 in steps of 5. So the branch now merges `main` and keeps upstream's structure and API as they are: `axis_scale(lo, hi, fmin, fmax, major, max_intervals, headroom)`, `Chart::axis_scale(secondary, max_intervals)`, `axis_range`, combo charts with a secondary axis, the room-based major unit, number formats and hidden axes. This PR's own `auto_scale` and its fixed "at most 10 intervals" unit rule are gone.

## What this adds on top of upstream
These are the documented rules for automatic axis limits (Microsoft's "How chart axis limits are determined", summarised by Jon Peltier) that `main` doesn't follow yet:

- **Automatic minimum:** `main` always starts the axis at zero. Office starts at zero only when every value is ≥ 0 and the smallest is below 5/6 of the largest. Otherwise the axis starts at the first major unit at or below `min − (max − min)/20`. Values of 85, 92 and 97 now get an 84–98 axis instead of bars that all look the same height.
- **All-negative data mirrors it:** the axis ends at zero only when the largest value is above 5/6 of the smallest. Otherwise it ends at the first major unit at or above `max + (max − min)/20`. (`main` didn't pad the top of an all-negative axis.) Mixed signs keep headroom at both ends, as on `main`.

author: Hevarh1

### Problem
When typing in Kurdish, Arabic, Hebrew or other right-to-left scripts in a new presentation, shape, or paragraph, the base direction was defaulting to Left-to-Right (`props.rtl: None` resolved to LTR, and paragraph alignment defaulted to `Align::Left`).
Under LTR base direction:
- The line was anchored at the left margin.
- Visual reordering placed each newly typed RTL character at the left edge of the run.
- The caret jumped back to the start of the line (left margin) on every keystroke, and jumped to the far right on space keys (due to UAX #9 rule L1).

### Solution
1. **UAX #9 Rule P2/P3 Auto-Detection**: Added `deckcraft_model::bidi::first_strong_is_rtl` to determine if a paragraph's first strong directional character belongs to an RTL script (Arabic, Kurdish, Hebrew, Syriac, Thaana, etc., or directional marks `\u{200F}`).

3. **Interactive Typing Promotion**: In `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs` (`insert_text`, `paste_body`, `set`), when inserting text into a paragraph with unassigned direction (`props.rtl.is_none()`), if the paragraph starts with an RTL character, it is automatically promoted to RTL (`props.rtl = Some(true)` and `props.align = Some(Align::Right)`), matching PowerPoint / Word behavior and persisting to PPTX/JSON. title: macOS: build the DMG with hdiutil create so the app passes codesign --strict
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #50.

`hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` puts a `com.apple.FinderInfo` on every file it writes into the image. The app is signed before that, so DeckCraft.app inside the released DMG, and any `ditto` copy of it, fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict` with "resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed". The script only re-checked the DMG's own signature after imaging, so this went unnoticed.

This is the fix PdfCraft and LightCraft already shipped (https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/823, https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/959), ported to `packaging/macos/package.sh`:

- The image is built with `hdiutil create -srcfolder … -fs HFS+ -format UDZO` instead of `makehybrid` + `convert`. `create` attaches a device while it copies and can hit "Resource busy" on CI runners, so it gets up to five tries with growing pauses.
- `xattr -cr` on the bundle before signing, so nothing picked up during the build ends up under the signature.
- After the DMG is signed, the script mounts it read-only and runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the app inside and on a `ditto` copy of it, plus `spctl --assess` on the copy when notarizing. Any failure stops the release and prints the app's xattrs.
- The volume name stays `DeckCraft` and `.DS_Store` / `.background` are copied as before, so the window layout is unchanged.
- `packaging/macos/dmg/README.md` no longer says the DMG is built with `makehybrid`.

Testing: I don't have a Mac, so this was not run. I checked the script with `bash -n` and shellcheck 0.11 (clean) and compared it line by line with the PdfCraft change, which was verified on macOS (the new gate passes, and fails with the old `makehybrid` lines put back). The release workflow's macOS job is what will actually exercise it; the new check after imaging makes that job fail loudly if something is off.

title: Windows: compile DX12 shaders with FXC
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
On Windows the app quit right after the window appeared with "Parent device is lost". wgpu's default DX12 shader compiler (`Auto`) loads whichever `dxcompiler.dll` it finds on the DLL search path. DeckCraft ships none, and without a matching `dxil.dll` DXC warns that the DXIL is unsigned. wgpu treats that warning as a compile error, its indirect-validation pipeline fails and the device is lost.

The fix sets the DX12 compiler to FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows) in `graphics::configure`, next to the existing DX12-only backend default. `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` still overrides it for troubleshooting, the same way `WGPU_BACKEND` overrides the backends. This is the same change as storytold/cadcraft#613 (and storytold/lightcraft#484, storytold/gridcraft#382). The README's Windows troubleshooting section mentions it.

Tested with a unit test in graphics.rs that starts from `Auto` and checks `configure` leaves FXC. It failed before the change and passes now, and a second test checks an explicit compiler choice is kept. `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (all 6 steps).

Not verified: I built on Linux only, where the `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` call in main.rs isn't compiled (no Windows target installed here), so Windows CI is what checks that line. Nobody ran it on a Windows machine.

title: PDF: map each glyph to its shaping cluster's text in ToUnicode (#164)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #164.

The PDF text layer gave each glyph its text range by position. That worked only when a run had exactly one glyph per character. When a run had fewer or more glyphs than characters (for example a ligature such as "fl"), glyph 0 got the whole run's text and every other glyph got nothing. The ToUnicode CMap then mapped one glyph to a whole sentence and left codes like `<0002>` with no mapping. poppler rejected the long entries, and text extraction came out garbled.

The cluster data the issue asks for is already available: `GlyphRun.cells` holds, for each glyph, the paragraph character that heads its shaping cluster. The new helper `glyph_text_ranges` uses it:

- A cluster runs from its head to the next cluster head in the run, or to the end of the run. A ligature glyph therefore maps to all of its characters ("fl" maps to `f` and `l`), and every other glyph maps to its own character.
- All glyphs of one cluster (for example a base letter and a combining mark, or kashida fill) share the cluster's range. krilla treats glyphs with the same range as one cluster and writes the text only once.
- Ranges are computed from cluster heads, not from glyph order, so right-to-left runs (glyphs in visual order) get the correct characters too. krilla then marks them as reversed.
- A glyph with no cell gets an empty range, the same as the old code gave it. Every range stays inside the run's text, so krilla's `text[range]` cannot panic.

Rendering does not change, because the text layer is invisible.

Test: `glyph_ranges_follow_shaping_clusters` in `crates/pdf/src/tests.rs` covers an "fl" ligature, a two-glyph cluster, and a right-to-left run that starts mid-paragraph and uses multi-byte characters. With the old logic, the ligature case maps the whole word to glyph 0.

title: CLI: --help prints usage and unknown render flags are rejected (#163)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #163.

`deckcraft-cli render --help` wrote a PNG named `--help`, because `render()` sent every unrecognised `--flag` to its catch-all arm, which made it the output path. A misspelled flag such as `--scael` was handled the same way.

Each point of the issue:

- **`render --help` / `-h`** now print the usage and exit 0 without touching the filesystem.
- **Unknown `render` options** (anything starting with `-` that is not a known flag) now fail with ``unknown option `--scael` ``, the same error `run` already gives for its unknown options.
- **`info`, `convert`, `run`, `commands`** print the usage and exit 0 on `--help` / `-h`, instead of opening a file called `--help`, complaining about missing arguments, or filtering the command list by "--help".
- **Top-level `deckcraft-cli --help` / `-h` / `help`** print the usage to stdout and exit 0. Running with no arguments or an unknown subcommand still prints it to stderr and exits 1.
- **`describe`, `app`, `mcp`** had the same problem (`describe --help` said "unknown command", `app --help` tried to reach the app, `mcp --help` said "unknown mcp option"), so they now take `--help` / `-h` too.

All of them print the full usage block, which is the only help text the CLI has.

Tests in `apps/deckcraft-cli/src/main.rs`:

- `render_help_prints_usage_and_writes_nothing`: `render --help` and `render -h` succeed and no `--help` file is created.
- `render_rejects_unknown_flag`: `render --sample --scael 2 out.png` returns the unknown-option error and writes nothing.
- `other_subcommands_accept_help`: `info`, `convert`, `run`, `describe` and `mcp` accept `--help` / `-h`.

- **Bounded line reads:** each line is read with `take(MAX_LINE + 1).read_until(b'\n', …)`. A line longer than `MAX_LINE` = 256 MiB (generous, since requests can carry documents or media as base64) gets an error reply and the connection is closed, without buffering the rest. Previously there was no line limit at all.
- **Connection cap:** at most `MAX_CONNECTIONS` = 16 connections are served at once; further ones get `{"ok": false, "error": "too many control connections"}` and are closed. A slot is released when its connection ends, including if its thread can't start or panics (`Drop` guard).

Everything else in request handling is unchanged (blank lines skipped, same replies, same timeouts). The approach mirrors DesignCraft's control server.

title: Slides: Ctrl+A in the slide pane selects every slide (#188)
author: isaac-levine
body:
Clicking in the slide thumbnails and pressing Ctrl+A (Cmd+A on a Mac) now selects every slide, like PowerPoint does. Before this the shortcut always ran `edit.selectAll`, which selects the shapes on the current slide no matter where you clicked.

`edit.selectAll` now takes an optional `scope: "slides"`, the same convention `edit.cut`, `edit.copy`, `edit.paste` and `edit.delete` already use. With it, every slide is selected (hidden ones too), shape and text selection is cleared, and the current slide stays where it is so the canvas doesn't jump. Any other scope value is an error, and so is calling it while a master or layout is being edited. Without a scope nothing changes.

I didn't reuse the `slides_scope` heuristic from `edit.delete`. The selection normally contains the current slide, so that heuristic would have hijacked Ctrl+A on the canvas too. Since the engine can't see which pane has focus, the UI tracks it: `SlideApp::slides_focused` follows the last primary click (inside the thumbnail pane or not), the sorter always counts, and `menus::ui_shortcut` sends the scoped command in that case.

Tests: engine tests for one slide, several slides with one hidden, the current slide staying put, the unscoped path being unchanged, and a bad scope returning an error. An egui_kittest test clicks a thumbnail, presses Cmd+A and checks all three slides are selected, then clicks the canvas and checks Cmd+A selects shapes again.

fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine -p deckcraft-ui-egui`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` all pass, and `cargo xtask parity` produced no changes. I haven't taken a screenshot of the running app, the kittest harness is the only UI coverage.

title: Animation effects: follow the system's reduced-motion setting
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Problem

With animation effects switched off in the OS (Windows 11: Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ Visual effects ▸ Animation effects), DeckCraft still animated its own interface: wheel scrolling and Ctrl+wheel zooming eased in over several frames, and menus, tooltips and dialogs faded in.

## What this changes

DeckCraft's own motion now follows the system setting by default, with an override in Preferences.

With effects off:

- A wheel notch scrolls the slide, the thumbnails, the Slide Sorter and every list by the whole notch at once.
- Ctrl/⌘+wheel zooms the slide and the Slide once.
- Menus, tooltips and dialogs don't fade in, and scroll areas don't glide to a target.
- A setting changed while DeckCraft is running is followed without a restart.

Where the setting is read:

| Platform | Source |
|---|---|
| Windows | Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ Visua (`UISettings.AnimationsEnabled`) |
| macOS | Accessibility ▸ Display ▸ Reduce motion (`NSWorkspace`) |
| Linux / BSD | XDG settings portal (`reduced-motion`, GNOME `enable-animations`, KDE `AnimationDurationFactor`), falling back to `kdeglobals` and GTK `settings.ini` where no portal answers |
| Web | `prefers-reduced-motion` media query |

Where the system reports nothing, animations

## Interface

- **Preferences ▸ Animation effects:** Use system setting (default), On, Off. While it follows the system, the dialog  shows what was detected.
- **Command:** `view.animationEffects` takes `{mode: "system"|"on"|"off"}` or `{on: bool}` (toggles without either) and answers `{mode, on, system}`.
- **Control channel:** `ui.set` accepts `animationEffects`; `ui.inspect` reports `animationsOn` and `systemAnimations`.
- **Saved state:** `animationEffects` in `ui.json`. An older file, or an unreadable value, loads as Use system setting without losing the other preferences.

## Not affected

What a presentation plays — transitions, slide animations, animated GIFs, video — is its content and runs as authored. Set Up Slide Show ▸ Show…

title: PPTX: SmartArt and OLE objects we can't draw keep their parts on save (#203)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes the data loss in #203 (both reproductions).

**Cause**: an object DeckCraft doesn't model (`ShapeKind::Opaque`) kept its `graphicFrame` XML, but not the parts that XML references. On save, any frame with relationship references was written as its preview picture or an empty rectangle — so `ppt/diagrams/*` and `ppt/embeddings/oleObject*.bin` were dropped.

**Fix**
- `Opaque` gets `parts: Vec<(rel id, relationship type, MediaId)>` (serde default, so existing `.deckcraft` files load unchanged). The reader fills it with every part the frame's XML references.
- The writer re-adds those parts under fresh slide relationship ids and rewrites the ids in the kept XML. If any reference can't be satisfied it falls back exactly as before (preview + `log::warn!`).
- `opc::Rel` now also keeps the full relationship type URI, so non-`officeDocument` types are written back correctly.
- **SmartArt**: a diagram's data part names its cached drawing by a *slide* relationship id (`dsp:dataModelExt relId`), which a save renumbers. That link is dropped from the kept data part. Only diagrams whose drawing is missing or empty reach this path (otherwise the drawing is already imported as a group).
- **Legacy OLE**: these objects find their preview in the slide's VML drawing through `spid`. DeckCraft doesn't write that drawing, and PowerPoint refuses to open a file with a dangling `spid`. The reader now takes the preview from the VML drawing (so DeckCraft shows it too), and the writer emits PowerPoint's own fallback form: no `spid`, preview as `p:pic`.

title: CLI, MCP and control channel answer agents in words
author: hoblin
body:
An AI agent driving `deckcraft-cli` reads its answers as is. Many of them didn't say what happened: a wrong command name was reported as broken JSON, a missing shape didn't say which or where, `null` didn't say what changed, and unknown parameter keys were silently ignored. Each one cost the agent extra turns on every deck.

Now every answer reads like a sentence written for a person. An error says how the CLI read the input, what is wrong with it, and the form that works, taken from the command's own params doc. It never guesses what the agent meant.

## Before and after

Real calls; "before" is `main`, "after" is this branch.

### 1. The command name

The agent wants a new blank presentation. It read `ID` in the help, `--cmd ID=JSON`, as a label of its own.

```
wrong:  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'new=file.new={"blank":true}'
right:  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'file.new={"blank":true}'

before: deckcraft-cli: new: bad JSON: expected ident at line 1 column 2
after:  deckcraft-cli: --cmd 1 of 1 was read as command `new` with parameters `file.new={"blank":true}`.
        `new` is not a command: --cmd takes COMMAND=PARAMS, a command id, then `=`, then a JSON object,
        e.g. --cmd 'slide.new={"title":"Q3"}'. Nothing ran.
```

### 2. A shape on another slide

The agent resizes a shape it drew on slide 0 after `slide.new` moved it to slide 1. Shape ids are looked up on the slide being edited.

```
wrong:  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'shape.insert={…}' --cmd slide.new --cmd 'shape.resize={"ids":[260],"w":50}' --save deck.deckcraft
right:  … --cmd 'slide.go={"index":0}' --cmd 'shape.resize={"ids":[260],"w":50}' …

before: deckcraft-cli: invalid parameters for `shape.resize`: no such shape
after:  deckcraft-cli: --cmd 3 of 3: shape 260 is on slide index 0, but shape ids are looked up on slide index 1,
        the one being edited; slide.go {"index": 0} switches to slide index 0. Nothing was saved or exported.
```

`edit.select`, `edit.delete`, `arrange.*` and every other command…

title: Animations: nine PowerPoint exit effects import as themselves (#147)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #147: PowerPoint exit animations losing their motion and direction on import.

**What the issue's video shows** (frames checked): the buildings use **Float In** to enter and a **Float Out** with the *Float Down* option to leave. | Float Out, Float Down (47) | `floatOut` + `d` | — |

title: Title bar: on macOS the window buttons sit centred in it (#71)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #71.

On macOS the window extends into the title bar and AppKit draws the traffic lights itself; moving them would need AppKit calls (`unsafe`), so the title bar has to fit them instead. DeckCraft's bar was 38 pt tall, so the lights sat 3 pt above its centre line. On macOS the bar is now 32 pt, centred on the lights, the quick-access buttons start after the three lights with the same gap the lights keep from the top (78 pt, was a fixed 84), and the Present button drops from 26 to 22 pt to keep a margin. Linux, Windows and web are unchanged (`TITLE_H` stays 38 pt).

The approach is the one from wordcraft #255 and gridcraft #323, but the constants were measured on a real macOS 27 window: lights 14 pt across, 23 pt centre to centre, the first at x = 9 pt, centred 16 pt from the top. Those PRs use 12 / 20 / 10 (a 28 pt band), which matches macOS 15 and earlier; on macOS 26+ that leaves the lights about 2 pt below the bar's centre and the first button about 1 pt from the green light. Happy to send the same follow-up to both. With this PR, on macOS 15 and earlier (12 pt lights centred at 14 pt) the lights would sit about 2 pt above the bar's centre, with a wider gap before the first button.

Validation:
- Ran the app on macOS 27 (Apple silicon) and captured the real window before and after (attached). After: 32 pt bar, lights centred on it, quick-access icons centred within 0.5 pt of them, 9 pt between the green light and the Home button.
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui --lib title_bar_tests`: a geometry test that fails if the macOS bar goes back to 38 pt, the content inset back to 84 pt or the Present button back to 26 pt.
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo xtask wasm` (macOS 27, Apple silicon).

I have before/after captures of the real window if they help; happy to attach them.

title: Text: draw shrink-on-overflow at the scale the file was saved with
author: xmaks82
body:

title: Canvas: drag the frame of a text box being edited to move it
author: pierrevbc
body:
## Problem

Once a text box or placeholder is in text editing, it can't be dragged: every press inside its
box, border included, places the caret or starts a text selection. A click on an unselected text

extra step: click outside, then drag it before the click turns into editing. In PowerPoint,
grabbing the border of a box being edited moves it, with the move cursor on hover.

1. `deckcraft --sample`, click into the title of slide 1: the caret appears.
2. Press on the title's dashed border and drag: the caret moves or text gets selected; the title

title: PDF export: vector slides with real text; effects rasterize per element
author: pierrevbc

title: MCP: confine file access with --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root
author: isaac-levine
body:
`deckcraft-cli mcp` gives the agent on the other end the same file access as the user running it. VectorCraft already has two flags for this, so this adds the same ones here with the same names and behaviour, and one client config works across the apps. It is the same change as storytold/gridcraft#480 and storytold/wordcraft#798.

    deckcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

**How it works**

The engine only ever opens a user-named file in three places: `file.open`, the media read behind `insert.picture`, `insert.audio`, `insert.video` and `picture.change`, and the writer behind `file.save`, `file.saveAs` and `file.export`. Those now go through two small helpers, `io::read_file` and `io::write_file`, and the checks sit there. The new `crates/engine/src/file_access.rs` holds the roots and the path logic: make the path absolute, follow symlinks (for a file that doesn't exist yet, resolve its nearest existing ancestor and require the rest to be plain names), then compare with the root by whole path components. On Windows the comparison ignores case, handles `\\?\` and UNC prefixes, and refuses device names like `CON` and `NUL`. Refusals come back as ordinary tool errors with VectorCraft's wording, for example `automation path rejected: outside the read root /work/project: /etc/passwd`.

title: `.deck` folder format: a presentation as one JSON file per slide, for Git
author: pierrevbc
body:
Closes #220.

## Problem

A `.deckcraft` file is a zip whose `presentation.json` is one compact line. In Git it is an opaque
binary: no readable diff, no review, and two branches that touch the same deck conflict on the
whole file. Decks edited by agents through the CLI or MCP leave changes nobody can review.

## What changes

A second on-disk form of the same document, a folder that DeckCraft opens and saves directly
(spec: `docs/deck-folder-format.md`):

```text
talk.deck/
├── deck.json             format, version, the presentation fields not stored elsewhere
├── slides.order          slide order and sections, one slide key per line
├── slides/<ULID>.json    one slide per file
├── masters/<id>.json     one master with its layouts and theme (+ notes.json, handout.json)
├── media-meta/<id>.json  {"id", "name", "contentType", "link"?, "sha256"}
└── media/<sha256>.<ext>  media bytes, named by content

1. **Format** (`crates/format/src/folder/`): `to_folder(&Presentation, previous) -> FileMap` and

title: Text: exact line spacing ends at the last line's descent
author: xmaks82
body:
With exact line spacing (`<a:lnSpc><a:spcPts/>`) PowerPoint puts the baseline at 80 % of the line pitch and ends the text at the last line's descent rather than a full pitch below it. We laid every line out a full pitch tall, so cells and text boxes using exact spacing came out taller than PowerPoint's: a table of 12 pt rows at 26.59 pt exact spacing (common in decks built from Excel tables) grew to 35.6 pt rows where PowerPoint draws 33 pt, pushing the table down and making shrink-on-overflow kick in early.

`layout_scaled`: under `Spacing::Pts` the baseline is at `0.8 × pitch` and `content_height` ends at the last line's descent (proportional and single spacing unchanged).

**Measured** against PowerPoint's own PDF of a real deck (`pdftotext -bbox`): rows now 33.5 pt vs PowerPoint's 32.9–33.8 pt (were 35.6). Across 31 decks / 597 slides the change touches 7 slides, all within ±1.5 of 255 per pixel.

Test: `exact_line_spacing_ends_at_the_last_descent` (fails before). `cargo test` for text/render/pptx/model and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

Side note while testing: `engine::tests::clicks_in_flipped_shapes_hit_the_text_where_it_is_drawn` fails ~3 in 10 full `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine` runs on `main` here (Linux, without craft-fonts, Liberation Sans): the click at x=240 lands on a character boundary and resolves to char 1 or char 2 between the plain and the flipped measurement, with the same face both times.
