title: Pictures: the black-and-white (bi-level) recolour is read, drawn and saved (#234)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #234.

`a:biLevel` on a picture's blip is now read into a new `PictureAdjust::bilevel` threshold (0–1, from `thresh` in 1/1000 of a percent, so `25000` = 25%), written back on save, and applied when the picture is decoded: each pixel whose luminance (Rec. 601 weights, the same ones the grayscale adjustment already uses) is below the threshold becomes black, the rest white, and alpha is left untouched, as ECMA-376 Part 1 describes the effect. It is applied after brightness/contrast/saturation and is part of the decoded-image cache key, so the same picture with and without the effect does not share a cached pixmap. The cyan-on-transparent logo from the issue now renders white over its cyan background.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-render --lib images` — new pixel test (cyan with alpha → white at a 25% threshold and black at 70%, dark blue → black, grey just above/below the threshold, alpha kept) and a cache-key test
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-pptx --test roundtrip` — the round-trip picture now carries `bilevel: Some(0.25)`
- each new test fails with the fix reverted and passes with it
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-model -p deckcraft-pptx -p deckcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Render: a group's child-coordinate scale no longer scales line widths (#233)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #233

## Cause

A group's children are drawn under `parent * group_child_affine(group, child_frame)`, which maps the group's child coordinate space onto its box. A deck from the old master-unit era uses a tiny child space (here `chExt` 3721 x 1910 against an `ext` of 5907087 x 3032125, a scale of about 1587), so that mapping scales by ~1587. `stroke()`, `arrowheads()` and the ink strokes in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` set that full transform on the context and give the line width in points, so a 0.75 pt line was stroked about 1200 pt wide and covered the slide. PowerPoint keeps line widths absolute: only the slide/view scale changes them.

## Fix

The renderer remembers the transform a top-level shape is drawn under (the slide-to-pixels view). For a shape inside a group, the outline is first carried through the rest of the chain (`view⁻¹ · m`) and then stroked under the view itself. So the group's child-coordinate scale moves and sizes the outline but never the line width, dash lengths (they are multiples of the width) or arrowhead size, also for groups scaled unevenly (100 across, 50 down). Shapes outside groups take exactly the code path they had (`m` itself, outline untouched).

## Verified

Offscreen with `deckcraft-cli render`: a deck made with the sample deck plus a group with the issue's child space (`off 284957,2284419`, `ext 5907087 x 3032125`, `chOff 1111,1899`, `chExt 3721 x 1910`) holding a 0.75 pt red line with an arrowhead and a 0.75 pt blue dashed rectangle.

| | rendered slide |
|---|---|
| `main` | covered by a huge red and blue shape |
| this branch | thin red diagonal line with its arrowhead and a thin dashed rectangle over the normal slide |

New test `tests::group_child_scale_does_not_scale_line_widths` in `crates/render/src/tests.rs`. It draws the same group (dashed 4 pt rectangle, 3 pt arrowed line, 5 pt ink stroke) with children laid out 1:1, in a child space of scale 100, and in one scaled unevenly, and requires the same number of inked…

title: Fonts: a family loaded by another thread is still found
author: xmaks82
body:
Two threads resolving the same installed family at once raced in `FontDb`:

1. The thread that lost found every face already added by the other, so `load_cataloged` returned "nothing added", `try_family` treated the family as missing, and the lookup fell through the substitutes to the last-resort face — the text was then drawn in whatever system font covered it (Ubuntu, here, instead of Liberation Sans).
2. Faces were pushed one at a time, so a lookup could see a family half-loaded (Bold before Regular, in path order) and take the wrong face.

**Fix** (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`): `try_family` looks again after loading whenever the family is installed, whoever loaded it; a file's (and a family's) faces are parsed first and added under one write lock, skipping duplicates.

**Why it matters beyond tests:** the app renders thumbnails/slides on several threads, so a deck opened right after start-up could lay out a text box in a fallback font (different widths, wraps and autofit) depending on timing.

**Flaky tests it explains:** `engine::tests::clicks_in_flipped_shapes_hit_the_text_where_it_is_drawn` failed 3 in 10 full `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine` runs on `main` here (Linux, no craft-fonts) — now 0 in 20; text-layout tests comparing two layouts in one test were affected the same way.

**Test:** `a_family_loaded_by_another_thread_is_still_found` copies an installed multi-face family to a temp folder and resolves it from 8 threads on a fresh `FontDb` 30 times (skips on a machine without such a family): fails 5/5 before, passes 10/10 after. `cargo test --workspace` and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

title: Text: line spacing reduction comes off the percentage, not the spacing
author: xmaks82
body:
PowerPoint's `lnSpcReduction` takes percentage points off a paragraph's line spacing (90 % less 20 % is 70 %) and leaves the space before/after paragraphs alone. We multiplied (90 % × 0.8 = 72 %) and shrank the paragraph spacing too, so shrunk text had different line and paragraph pitches from PowerPoint's.

**Measured** on PowerPoint's own PDF of a real deck (`pdftotext -bbox`): a body at 90 % spacing, 10 pt before paragraphs, `fontScale=85%`, `lnSpcReduction=20%` runs at 20.2 pt lines (23.8 pt × ~1.2 × 0.70) with 9.9 pt between paragraphs.

`layout_scaled`: `Pct(f)` lines are `natural × (f − reduce)` (floored at 10 % of f); `spacing_pts` no longer applies the reduction. With #226 (saved scale), 10 of 12 affected slides across 31 decks get closer to PowerPoint.

Test: `line_spacing_reduction_comes_off_the_percentage` (fails before). `cargo test` for text and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

title: Text: honour spcFirstLastPara (space before the first paragraph)
author: xmaks82
body:
`<a:bodyPr spcFirstLastPara="1">` makes the first paragraph's space before and the last paragraph's space after count. PowerPoint honours it (and Google Slides exports set it on every body); we always dropped both, so such text sat one paragraph gap too high — 9.5 pt on a real deck, measured against PowerPoint's PDF.

- Model: `BodyProps::space_first_last`, inherited like the other body properties (default false in `resolve::body`).
- Read/write `spcFirstLastPara`.
- Layout: the first paragraph's space before and the last one's space after count when it's set.

Across 31 real decks this (with the other text fixes) moved 47 slides closer to PowerPoint's rendering.

Tests: `space_before_the_first_paragraph_with_spc_first_last_para` (text), `body_props` extended (pptx). `cargo test` for text/pptx/model/render and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

title: fix(cli): render refuses an unknown option instead of writing it as a file (#235)
author: RCShoemaker
body:
## What was wrong
`deckcraft-cli render` treated any argument it didn't recognise as the output path. So `render deck.pptx --help` rendered the slide into a PNG named `--help` (#235), and a mistyped option such as `--bogus` was silently ignored.

Reproduced on `main` at `688c7ef`:
```
$ deckcraft-cli render --sample --help
--help (1920×1080)            # and a 111 KB file named --help
$ deckcraft-cli render --sample --bogus out.png
out.png (1920×1080)           # --bogus ignored, exit 0
```

## Fix
In `render`'s argument loop, an argument that starts with `-` and isn't a known option is now an error: `deckcraft-cli: unknown render option `--bogus``. A lone `-` still reaches the existing path handling.

## Relation to #228
#228 makes `--help` / `-h` print help for every subcommand, which covers the other half of #235. This PR only touches the render argument loop, which #228 leaves alone, so the two shouldn't conflict. With both merged, #235 is fully fixed. I've left #236 to #228, which documents that `--slide` counts from 0.

## Tests
- New `render_refuses_an_unknown_option_instead_of_writing_it_as_a_file` covers `--bogus`, `-x` and `--help` and checks that no file is written. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) on Windows 11.

author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built deckcraft and deckcraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.

title: Render: two-colour gradients ramp like PowerPoint's
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: a two-colour gradient (black to white, or any two theme colours) was blended linearly in sRGB, so it looked darker and muddier through the middle than in PowerPoint. Red to green went through brown.

After: two-colour gradients ramp like PowerPoint's, lighter and smoother through the middle. Gradients with three or more stops, or with a stop moved off an end, still blend linearly, because that is what PowerPoint does with them.

How: I built gradient probes in PowerPoint (five colour pairs, both directions, on shapes and on a slide background, three stops, a stop at 20 %) and read PowerPoint's exported pixels. A gradient of exactly two stops at 0 % and 100 % mixes the colours in linear light, with the second colour's share following an S-shaped curve: black to white is 105, 186 and 238 at a quarter, half and three quarters, against 64, 128 and 191 linearly. Anything else is linear in sRGB (black to red to white gives 64, 128, 191 per segment). The new `ramp` module holds the measured curve (symmetric, 17 points) and expands a two-colour gradient into 16 pieces, so vello's sRGB interpolation draws PowerPoint's ramp. Fills use it for linear and path gradients alike.

On 446 Apache POI slides, 6 got closer to PowerPoint's export (Office theme backgrounds: `backgrounds` slide 2 went from 11.2 to 4.7, `themes` slide 3 from 10.2 to 2.9) and one SmartArt slide moved by under a point.

Tests:
- `ramp::tests`: black to white and two colour pairs match PowerPoint's pixels within 3, the ends are the stops, the weight is symmetric and monotonic, and only two-colour gradients are expanded.
- `a_linear_gradient_ramps_like_powerpoint`, `a_gradient_with_a_stop_off_the_end_stays_linear` (render): rendered pixels at 25/50/75 % match PowerPoint.

title: Comments: threads and resolved state survive a .pptx round trip (#70)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #70.

**What was wrong.** The writer emitted the legacy comment part only, so replies were flattened into sibling comments and the resolved flag was dropped. Modern PowerPoint decks carry a second, threaded part (`p188`) as well — and the reader took both, importing every comment twice.

**Export** (`crates/pptx/src/write/mod.rs`): a slide with comments now also writes the modern threaded part `ppt/comments/modernCommentN.xml` — `p188:cmLst` with nested `p188:replyLst`, `status="resolved"`, EMU `p188:pos`, the slide's `commentRel` anchor ext and the modern `ppt/authors.xml` with GUID author ids — next to the flattened legacy part, the same pair of parts PowerPoint itself writes. Older readers keep the legacy view; PowerPoint 2021+ and DeckCraft read threads and resolved state.

**Import** (`crates/pptx/src/read/mod.rs`): when a slide carries both parts, the modern one wins and the flattened legacy copy is skipped (the dedup also covers packages that type the modern part through a `Default` entry — the `p188` root is recognized too). Modern positions scale as EMU; they were read as legacy 1/8 pt, ~1587× off, so markers from real PowerPoint decks land in the right place now.

Comment ids are deterministic GUIDs from the existing `tables::guid`, so exports stay reproducible with no new dependency.

**Known limitation for a follow-up:** comments anchor with `p188:unknownAnchor` (schema-valid) rather than a slide moniker, which needs part identity the model does not have yet.

**Format facts verified** against the Open XML SDK part registry and schema files (`PowerPointCommentPart.json`, `PowerPointAuthorsPart.json`, the 2018/8 schema), ONLYOFFICE's PPTX writer and Microsoft's add-comment sample: content types, rel type URIs, `CT_Comment` child order (anchor → pos → replyLst → txBody), required attributes, braced-GUID ids, `userId=""`/`providerId` handling, and the anchor ext URI.

title: Start screen: a missing Recent file is marked, its error shows, and entries can be removed (#172)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #172.

**What was wrong.** The start screen reported errors through `set_status`, but the status bar is only drawn while a presentation is open (`SlideApp::ui`): clicking a Recent entry whose file had moved or been deleted did nothing visible, and the same went for every other start-screen error, like a failed **Open the sample deck**.

**The fix** (`crates/ui-egui`):

- The start screen now draws the transient status message itself, right under the Open row — a real `Label`, not painted text, so screen readers see it too, and wrapped so a long OS error doesn't clip at the panel edge. Shared with the status bar through a new `SlideApp::fresh_status()` (peek-with-expiry), replacing the inline 6 s check there.
- Recent entries whose file no longer exists are dimmed with a `(missing)` mark and hover text **before** anything is clicked.
- Each Recent row gets a remove button (`SlideApp::forget_recent`), persisting with the usual prefs save.
- A successful open clears a stale error, so an old failure no longer lingers next to a document that just opened.

**Deliberate limits:** existence is probed once per path per session — a stat on a dead network share can block for the OS timeout, so UNC paths and URLs are never probed (they stay unmarked and are judged when opened); a disconnected mapped drive would still stall once, accepted. The remove button is a plain `×` because U+2715 has no glyph in the UI font stack (egui would draw the replacement character — visible in a first draft).

**Tests:** three kittest UI tests driving the real start screen — the missing mark and the drawn error (asserted through the accessibility tree, so a fix that paints the message invisibly would fail), removal from the list, and the negative case (an existing file is never marked). Visually verified via snapshot against both the broken and fixed rendering. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

body:

Before: tables drew in the wrong colours whenever their style wasn't one of a handful DeckCraft knows. Every unknown style (Themed, Light, Dark and most Medium variants) was drawn as Medium Style 2, so gradient-banded themed tables came out pale blue and white, and saving dropped the style definitions the file carried.

title: Chart legend: honour legendPos and overlay in the renderer (#262)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #262.

The reader kept `c:legend/c:legendPos` (default `r`) and the writer wrote it back, but `crates/render/src/chart.rs` always drew the legend as one row under the plot. Now the renderer places the legend by `legendPos`. The layout is in a small `legend_layout` function so that it can be tested:

- `r` (the OOXML default; unknown values fall back to it) and `l`: a vertical stack, centred vertically, and the plot area is narrowed on that side.
- `t` / `b`: a centred row, and the plot area gets shorter. `b` gives the same layout as before.
- `tr`: a vertical stack in the top-right corner, and the plot area is narrowed.
- `c:overlay val="1"`: the legend is drawn in the same place, but the plot area keeps its full size. The reader now reads `c:overlay` into a new `Chart::legend_overlay` field (default `false`), and the writer writes it back instead of always writing `0`.

Not in this PR: `c:legend/c:layout/c:manualLayout`. DeckCraft does not read `c:layout` for any chart element yet (the plot area's manual layout is also ignored). Handling it needs both `edge` and `factor` modes and a write-back, so it should be a separate change.

Tests:
- `render::chart::tests` checks the legend origin and the remaining plot area for `r`, `l`, `t`, `tr`, `b` (unchanged from before) and overlay.
- `read::chart::tests::legend_position_and_overlay_are_read` checks `legendPos`/`overlay`, and the defaults when they are missing (`r`, no overlay).

Neither test compiles on `main`: `legend_layout` and `legend_overlay` do not exist there.

Based on `main` and stands on its own. It replaces #219, and folds in #229's fix to this PR's own "not available" hint.

An AI agent driving `deckcraft-cli` reads its answers as is. Many of them didn't say what happened: a wrong command name was reported as broken JSON, a missing shape didn't say which or where, `null` didn't say what changed, and unknown parameter keys were silently ignored. title: macOS: end the process in on_exit so closing the window doesn't crash
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #279.

Same crash and same fix as storytold/gridcraft#117 (PR storytold/gridcraft#316, c1d293296), which followed storytold/vectorcraft#670. eframe runs with `run_and_return`, so it drops the window while AppKit's run loop is still going. AccessKit's macOS adapter gives the content view back its original class on teardown, and AppKit's Touch Bar support still has a KVO observation on it, so the next display cycle throws "not registered" and the app aborts. On macOS, `App::on_exit` now ends the process right after saving the preferences, before eframe tears the window down. eframe calls `on_exit` on every way out (close button, ⌘Q, `app.quit`), and only after the unsaved-changes prompt has let the window close, so Save / Don't Save still work as before. Nothing after it is needed: prefs are written and the log file is unbuffered. Windows and Linux are unchanged.

WordCraft (#539) and PhotoCraft (#1624) went a different way, quitting through `-[NSApplication terminate:]`. That needs objc2/dispatch2 in the app, so I kept GridCraft's one-liner. Happy to switch.

Validation:
- `on_exit_ends_the_process_on_macos` (new, in `apps/deckcraft/src/main.rs`): runs `on_exit` in a child copy of the test binary and checks the process ends inside it on macOS (and returns elsewhere). Fails on main (`on_exit returned` is printed), passes here
- I couldn't reproduce the crash itself on an M1 Pro with no Touch Bar: on main, the close button (AX `AXCloseButton`) and `app.quit` both exit 0 with no crash report. With the fix, both still exit 0, and `ui.json`, `prefs.json` and the log are still written
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS 27, Apple silicon)

body:

Before: Latin text was shaped with the font's default features, so Calibri drew "ti" (in "Autism", "Transformation"), "fi" and "ffi" as joined ligatures, and every run was pair-kerned even when the file turns kerning off (`kern="0"`) or the text is below the `kern` size.

After: Latin, Greek and Cyrillic text draws no standard or contextual ligatures, and pairs are kerned only when the run's `kern` size is set and the text reaches it, as PowerPoint does. On a test deck built in PowerPoint (Calibri, Cambria and Arial at 40 pt, kerning off and on), line widths now match PowerPoint's exactly; before, kerning-off lines were narrower and ligatures were visible.

How: `make_style` records whether the run kerns; items split on it; `shaping_features` turns off `kern` where the run doesn't kern, and `liga`/`clig` for alphabetic scripts. Arabic and other scripts keep their ligatures, and items with emoji sequences keep them too (they're joined by ligatures in some fonts). Tests cover the feature choice per script, a font with an ffi ligature drawing one glyph per letter, and kerning switching on at exactly the `kern` size (the font tests pick any installed font that has the ligature or kerns AVATAR).

title: fix(security): require a token on the control channel
author: mendy-cohen
body:
Fixes #263.

- New `deckcraft_mcp::auth` module. The token is `DECKCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN` if set, otherwise 32 random bytes from the OS. The app writes it to `deckcraft-control-<port>.token` in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or the per-user temp folder. The file is created fresh each start (never through an existing symlink) and is mode 0600 on Unix.
- The first request on a connection must be `auth` with the right token, compared in constant time. Anything else gets an error and the connection is closed, including a non-JSON first line like an HTTP request from a browser. A repeated `auth` after that is answered without reaching the UI.
- `Remote` (used by `deckcraft-cli app` and `mcp --connect`) sends the token on every connection. It looks the token up again on reconnect, so a restarted app still works.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` and `AGENTS.md` describe the handshake.

This is the same approach as storytold/gridcraft#834, and it lines up with what PhotoCraft and PdfCraft already do.

### Testing
- New unit tests: token generation and matching, token file permissions, and a real-socket test showing requests reach the UI only after `auth`.
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-mcp -p deckcraft`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on the touched crates, `cargo fmt` and `cargo xtask layers` all pass.
- Manual run on macOS with `deckcraft --control 7990`. A request with no token is refused, an HTTP-style request is refused, the token file is `-rw-------`, and `deckcraft-cli app --port 7990 --method ui.inspect` works.

title: fix(macos): open .pptx and .deckcraft files from Finder
author: mendy-cohen
body:
On macOS, DeckCraft can't be chosen as the default app for presentations, and double-clicking a file can't open it in DeckCraft.

**Why:** `Info.plist.in` declares the `.deckcraft` and `.pptx` UTIs but has no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, so LaunchServices doesn't know DeckCraft opens them. And Finder sends files as a `kAEOpenDocuments` Apple event, not as command-line arguments. winit 0.30 doesn't handle that event, so even with the plist fixed, the file never reached the app.

**Changes**
- `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`: adds `CFBundleDocumentTypes` for DeckCraft Presentation (`Owner`) and PowerPoint Presentation (`Alternate`, so existing apps stay preferred until the user picks DeckCraft).
- `apps/deckcraft/src/apple_events.rs`: the same approach as GridCraft's `apple_events.rs`. It registers the handler with `fmv-macos-events = "=0.1.0"` before the event loop starts and opens the paths on the next frame. Errors are logged and shown in the status bar. The dependency is the same pinned version and checksum as in GridCraft's `Cargo.lock`, and the workspace stays `forbid(unsafe_code)`.
- Ignores the `-psn_` argument older macOS adds on a Finder launch. It used to be treated as a file to open.

I only declared `.pptx` and `.deckcraft`. `file.open` sniffs content, so `.potx`/`.ppsx` might work too, but I didn't verify them.

### Testing
- `cargo build`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo xtask layers` and `plutil -lint` all pass.
- On macOS 26 (arm64) I built a throwaway bundle from the debug binary and this `Info.plist.in`, registered it with `lsregister`, and ran `open -a <bundle> "Test Deck.pptx"`, using a `.pptx` saved by `deckcraft-cli run --sample`. `ui.inspect` showed the deck open. `lsregister -dump` lists the claimed UTIs as `org.openxmlformats.presentationml.presentation, ai.storyteller.deckcraft.presentation`.
- I didn't run the full `packaging/macos/package.sh` (signing and notarization).

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

title: Text: Tab no longer ends text entry in lists (#93)
author: FabPei
body:
Pressing Tab to indent a list item killed the keyboard: the item gained a level, but no further typing, Enter, Backspace or arrow keys reached the text. The same happened after any arrow key during text editing, so pressing Enter to add a list item appeared to do nothing and new items never joined the list. Lists looked broken even though the text and list commands themselves behaved correctly.

The cause is the slide keyboard gate in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: Tab and arrow keys that no widget claims move egui's keyboard focus onto ordinary widgets (the window's drag handle, ribbon buttons), and `SlideApp::keyboard` dropped every key while any widget held focus — the focus cycle intercepted the keys from then on. #78 reports the same symptom from the Tab side.

While text on the slide is being edited, that stray keyboard focus is now surrendered before key handling, so the edited text keeps the keyboard. Real text fields, dialogs, the command palette and open menus keep their keys exactly as before.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, layering, assets, wasm). The new regression test `tab_in_an_edited_list_keeps_the_keyboard` drives a list through the real egui input path — type, Enter, Tab, type, Enter, type — and asserts the text and the list levels; it fails before this change because every key after Tab is swallowed.

Fixes storytold/deckcraft#93

title: Open: a password-protected presentation says so, and open errors show on the start screen
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #346.

A password-protected .pptx isn't a zip: PowerPoint stores it as a compound file (CFB) holding `EncryptionInfo` and `EncryptedPackage` streams. `open_presentation` didn't recognise it and returned the generic "not a presentation DeckCraft can read", and `pick_and_open` dropped that error with `let _ =`. title: Fonts: the font scan leaves out faces with no outline tables
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Problem

The font scan (`file_face_names` in `crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`) also lists faces with none of the tables skrifa reads glyph outlines from (`glyf`, `CFF `, `CFF2`, `VARC`), such as faces whose glyphs are bitmaps only or are stored as outlines in Apple's `hvgl` table. `FontDb::outline`, which the renderer reads glyph outlines from, returns an empty path for every glyph of such a face.

On macOS 27.0.1 the scan of `/System/Library/Fonts` catalogs "GB18030 Bitmap" (`Supplemental/NISC18030.ttf`), so it is in `FontDb::families()`, which the Home tab's font list shows. The face stores its glyphs as `bdat` bitmaps and has no color glyph tables. It maps 27,544 characters, `FontDb::outline` returns an empty path for all of them, and the renderer draws none of them (`crates/render/src/lib.rs:1487-1493`).

## Fix

`file_face_names` leaves out a face whose table directory has none of those four tables. vectorcraft has the same check (https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/781), and the open designcraft pull request https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/pull/443 adds it there. With the check, the scan of `/System/Library/Fonts` on the same Mac catalogs 785 faces instead of 786, and "GB18030 Bitmap" is the one left out.

## Test

`faces_without_outlines_are_not_cataloged` (`crates/fonts/src/lib.rs`) renames the `glyf` table of the `legacy-semibold.ttf` fixture in memory, writes it and a copy of `legacy-regular.ttf` to a temporary folder, and scans that folder. The Regular is listed, and the Semibold is listed under neither its typographic nor its Windows family name. On `main` the test fails (`styles("DeckCraft Legacy")` returns `["Regular", "Semibold"]`). title: Slides: Select All follows the pane - Ctrl+A over the slides pane or in the sorter takes every slide (#188)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #188.

**What was wrong.** Ctrl+A always ran the engine's `edit.selectAll`, which selects the current slide's shapes: clicking a thumbnail and pressing Ctrl+A looked like nothing happened.

**The fix** (`crates/ui-egui`, engine untouched): the UI keyboard path routes Cmd/Ctrl+A to `slide.selectSlides` with every slide while the pointer last worked the slides pane or in the Slide Sorter — Select All follows the pane, as in PowerPoint. On the canvas the engine keeps its shapes semantics, so MCP and the control channel are unchanged (they have no pane, and the Edit menu's Select All stays with the shapes like modern PowerPoint's Home ▸ Select).

**Design note:** an engine-level rule ("slides selected ⇒ select slides") was considered and rejected — `go_to` sets `sel.slides = [current]` on every navigation, so the ordinary canvas state would have made canvas Ctrl+A regress to selecting slides.

**Hardening against stale-flag paths** (each walked through in review):

- text being edited and slide-master context fall through to the engine (`selection.text.is_none()`, `target == Slides`);
- the flag only counts where the pane exists (Normal/Reading views);
- a canvas press collapses the pane's multi-selection back to the current slide — so pane Ctrl+A → canvas click → Delete can never sweep the deck with a second Delete;
- opening or creating a deck clears the flag.

**Known small gap:** the thumbnail pane draws its tiles with the painter (no accessibility nodes), so the flag-setting click itself isn't driven by the tests; the flag's effect, the canvas-press collapse (driven through a real `PointerButton` event on `canvas_rect`), and the sorter route are all covered. A natural follow-up, also noted in review: Delete/Backspace after a slide selection currently only honours the Delete key.

**Tests:** two kittest UI tests — the pane ⇄ canvas Select All round-trip including the real canvas press, and the sorter route. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: Bump quick-xml to 0.41 (RUSTSEC-2026-0194, RUSTSEC-2026-0195)
author: natocool2
body:
Bumps quick-xml from 0.38 to 0.41, which fixes two advisories:

- [RUSTSEC-2026-0194](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0194.html): `Attributes` with the default `with_checks(true)` takes O(N²) time on a start tag with N attributes.
- [RUSTSEC-2026-0195](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0195.html): `NsReader` allocates for every `xmlns` declaration on a tag with no limit.

**Exposure today: none that I can find.** `deckcraft-pptx` reads attributes with `with_checks(false)` and does not use `NsReader`. The bump clears `cargo audit`/`cargo deny` for anyone who ships DeckCraft, and leaves one copy of quick-xml in the lockfile instead of two.

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml`: `quick-xml = "0.41"`.
- `crates/pptx/src/xml.rs`: `decode_and_unescape_value(decoder)` is deprecated in 0.40+ (and `clippy -D warnings` would fail). It is replaced with `decoded_and_normalized_value(XmlVersion::Implicit1_0, decoder)`, which is the call the deprecated method now makes.

## How this was checked

- The quick-xml API used here was diffed between 0.38.4 and 0.41.0 (`Reader`/`Config` fields, `Event` variants, `BytesStart`/`BytesText`/`BytesRef`, `escape`): the only changes that touch this workspace are the deprecations above. `Attribute::normalized_value*` is exactly what the deprecated methods call in 0.41, so behaviour is the same as a plain bump. One difference from 0.38 that comes with the bump itself: attribute values now get XML 1.0 normalisation (a literal tab/CR/LF inside an attribute value becomes a space; `
` is kept), as the spec requires.
- `Cargo.lock` was updated with `cargo update --workspace` only: quick-xml 0.38.4 is removed and every dependent now points at the 0.41.0 already locked for `wayland-scanner`. No other package moves.
- `rustfmt --check` passes on the changed files. I did **not** build or run `cargo xtask ci` locally; CI here is the first compile, so please treat its result as the check.

_Requested by **Brandon**_

title: slide.new reads leading tabs in body as bullet levels; --help prints the usage (#360)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #360

## Cause

1. `slide.new` (MCP `add_slide`) builds the body with `TextBody::from_text`, which keeps a leading tab as a literal character in a level-1 paragraph. `text.set` has its own code that turns leading tabs into the outline level, so the same text gave different results through the two commands.
2. The desktop binary's argument loop knew `--control`, `--sample`, `--show` and `--version`; everything else, `--help` included, was pushed on the list of files to open, so it logged `--help: No such file or directory` and left the editor open.

## Fix

Two commits, one per report.

- `take_tab_level` (in `cmd/text.rs`) is the one rule for a leading tab (one level per tab, up to 8, dropped from the text). `text.set` uses it as before and `slide.new` now applies it to each paragraph of `body`. The title is not touched.
- `parse_args` reads the command line, and `-h` / `--help` print the usage (`--control`, `--sample`, `--show`, `--version`, `--help`) and exit, as `--version` does. Other arguments mean what they did.

## Verified

- On `main`, the test `a_new_slides_body_takes_leading_tabs_as_bullet_levels` (the issue's body `"Install from DMG\nLaunch app\n\tCheck signing\nBuild a deck"` plus a two-tab line) fails: the paragraphs come back as `(0, "\tCheck signing")` and `(0, "\t\tDeeper")`; with the fix they are `(1, "Check signing")` and `(2, "Deeper")`, the same as `text.set` gives for the same text (the test compares both). A body without tabs is unchanged.
- `help_prints_the_usage_instead_of_opening_a_file` and `the_other_arguments_still_mean_what_they_did` cover `parse_args` (the second one pins the existing flags, the environment port and a bad `--control` value). `cargo run -p deckcraft -- --help` now prints the usage and exits without opening a window.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo xtask assets`, `layers` and `wasm` pass.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 753 pass, 2 fail. Both fail on an unmodified `main` (`735e16d`…

title: ui: admit stock macOS CJK faces as interface fallbacks (#101)
author: Momentum96
body:
Follow-up to #331 (#101). On macOS, Korean text in the window title, recent files, outline and
notes still drew as boxes.

Cause: `uifonts.rs` skips borrowed faces over `MAX_FACE_BYTES` (48 MB). macOS's only Hangul face,
`/System/Library/Fonts/AppleSDGothicNeo.ttc`, is 55,323,000 bytes, so it was rejected; the font
database returns one face per character, so nothing else was tried. With that fixed, Simplified
Chinese hit the same wall: the picked face is `PingFang.ttc` at 78,222,888 bytes.

Fix: raise the cap to 128 MB (same bound as PhotoCraft), with a comment naming the largest stock
faces it must admit. No fonts bundled. Windows/Linux stock CJK faces are all under 48 MB, so
behaviour there is unchanged.

Reproduced on macOS: `ime_tests::cjk_text_in_the_interface_is_drawn_with_real_glyphs` failed with
`FontId{13, Proportional} draws "한국어발표자료" of "한국어 발표 자료" as boxes`; it now passes with all
four scripts checked.

Checks: `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui --lib` (45 passed), `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Not run locally: `cargo xtask wasm`.

Trade-off: egui keeps its own copy of each borrowed face, so a Mac UI showing Korean and Chinese
can hold up to ~133 MB more (only once such text is on screen).
